topics.topic: Failure precedence between forbidden plain HTTP and repeated required headers
questions: When both the plain-HTTP policy and required-header checks fail, which failure detail is returned first?
When both plain HTTP is forbidden and required headers are repeated, which failure must be returned first?
Which failure wins when both the plain-HTTP policy and repeated-required-header check fail?

quotes: `service_invoker.prepare_request` with that operation owns every instance failure — no selected instance, no `api_base_url`, a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed (A09 rules 1, 4 and 6) — resolves the credential through `installation` and places the inputs, in that order, naming the first failure.

`instance_address_missing`; then a plain `http` target not allowed, a repeated required header, an invalid required header (`required_header_invalid`, A08 rule 5), then the credential, then input placement, input ports in name order and a list's elements in list order, the first that cannot be placed named (A09 rules 1, 2, 4, 6);
judgement.why: State 3 puts repeated headers before forbidden plain HTTP, while State 5 puts forbidden plain HTTP first.

topics.topic: Which selected or credentialed services have manifests validated at startup
questions: Which services are checked at start when a service has a selected instance but no configured credential?
Must startup read and validate the manifest record of every service with a selected instance, or only services having configured credentials?
At startup, are manifest records checked for every selected service, every credentialed service, or only their intersection?

quotes: A selected service whose manifest record cannot be read stops the start naming it; a selected instance the record does not list fails nothing here (it is not invocable at send, A09 rule 6).

The services checked are those the installation holds a credential for, in `service_id` code-point order; for each, the kernel-set names are compared first, without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for it, its manifest record is read and that instance's required headers compared.
judgement.why: One passage requires checking every selected service, while the other limits the checked services to those with credentials.

topics.topic: Exact future sends authorized by a standing approval grant
questions: Is the operation's stated effect qualified by all class and resend exceptions, or is a grant intended to authorize every later send of the node?
What exact future sends does a newly granted approval authorize?

quotes: A later send of that node in a run pinned to that version uses the grant as its authority only where step 2 lets it: a `state-transition` or `external-effect` send with no matching unused approval, not a resend after `not_applied`; a grant for a `read` or `draft-write` node is never used (M25, A10 rule 6).
judgement.why: The text expressly limits grant authority by effect class, existing approval and resend status.

topics.topic: Owner access operation for reading trial-case fixture bytes
questions: Can the owner read the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?
Can the owner read the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?

quotes: Records reach a caller as they are (State 3), with values resolved by `module:surface`: a `value` StoredValue as its JSON content; a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`.

`read_spooled_file` takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue — and names it by its identity — `run_id`, `producer_node_id`, `map_index` (omitted for a node that is not mapped), `attempt_number`, `producer_port`, `list_index` (omitted for a `one` port) — the lookup identity and the request's only fields; its digest, size and media type are not asked, they come back in the answer.
judgement.why: The owner is promised every value, but fixture bytes are restricted to an operation that expressly rejects their StoredValue representation.

topics.topic: Pagination semantics when records enter or leave mutable filters between pages
questions: What happens when the boundary record, or another record below it, changes into or out of a mutable filter such as `status` between pages?
What happens when records enter or leave a status-filtered list between pages, including when the record at the token's position no longer matches the filter?

judgement.divergence: One implementer preserves the first page's filtered membership and continues below the saved position even if statuses change; another re-evaluates the mutable filter, potentially rejecting a token whose boundary record left the filter and including or omitting records that changed status. The caller notices an `invalid_request` or different records and omissions across pages.
judgement.why: The token position is defined, but membership and token validity after in-place changes to filtered fields are not.

topics.topic: Representation that lets canonical JSON serialization detect duplicate object keys
questions: How can this operation detect and refuse duplicate object keys after its input has already become a JSON value?
What representation reaches `canonical_bytes` so it can detect duplicate object member names before an ordinary JSON parser has discarded them?

judgement.why: The representation and parsing boundary that preserves duplicate JSON members is an encoding and field-type question assigned to State 6.

topics.topic: Whether successful release or cancellation waits for physical spool deletion
questions: Does a successful release or cancellation guarantee physical deletion before returning, or only make the spool logically inaccessible while deletion may be deferred?
Does successful release or cancellation guarantee physical deletion before returning, or only make the spool logically inaccessible and schedule best-effort deletion?

quotes: The run's spooled files are gone.
A spool that cannot be removed does not fail the request: the release is recorded, and the spool of a released run is removed at the next start (A18 rule 4).
judgement.why: One passage guarantees the files are gone on successful release, while the other permits successful return with physical deletion deferred.

topics.topic: Atomicity or cleanup of content-addressed bytes when record changes fail
questions: If publishing value or fixture bytes succeeds but the record change fails, must the unreferenced bytes be removed, retained as inert orphans, or committed atomically with the record?

topics.topic: Cleanup of files spooled before a later attempt or record-update failure
questions: If an attempt has already spooled earlier files and a later file or the subsequent record change fails with `internal_error`, what operation removes the earlier unrecorded files, and when?

topics.topic: Exact sandbox probe behavior and startup refusal criteria
questions: What exact code, inputs, bounds, expected output and isolation properties constitute the probe, and which failed observation makes start-up refuse?

topics.topic: How approval previews represent request data containing personal inputs
questions: How is a built URL, query, JSON body, or multipart description returned to an agent when it embeds a `personal_data` input?

topics.topic: How trial-case file bytes and metadata are supplied, computed, and verified
questions: For authored file inputs or expected file outputs, does the operation receive file bytes, only digest/size/media-type facts, or both, and who computes and verifies those facts before persistence?

topics.topic: Identity definition for a SpooledFile
questions: Is SpooledFile identity the producing position alone, or the complete M22 fact set including content facts?

topics.topic: Machine-readable refusal reason values for public operations
questions: What exact machine-readable reason values may accompany `refused` for each public operation?

topics.topic: Ownership of copying failed-execution spool files into fixtures
questions: Which module reads and copies spooled file bytes into the fixture area, and therefore owns copy failures and cleanup?

topics.topic: Persistence location for actor attribution when records lack an actor field
questions: Where is the acting actor persisted for records whose State 1 model has no actor field?

topics.topic: Required completeness of trial-case input and expected-output port maps
questions: Must authored `inputs` contain exactly every input port and no extra names, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it contain exactly every output port, or may it be partial?

topics.topic: Response-body size enforcement for bindings without output ports
questions: For a binding without output ports, must the response body still be read and counted up to `service_response_bytes_max`, and does exceeding it produce `contract_violation`, despite the body being described as ignored?

topics.topic: Source of the schema for flow constants
questions: Does `compose_flow_version` require each constant to declare its own `value_schema`, or is the schema taken from its target port?

topics.topic: Startup validation of installation invariants and validation order
questions: Does start-up also validate the earlier required installation invariants that are absent here, including unique agent names and a credential header that is an HTTP field-name token, and in what order?

topics.topic: Whether a direct not-applied 4xx attempt can be resent
questions: Can a direct 4xx attempt recorded `not_applied` ever be resent, or does the run fail permanently without a resend operation?

topics.topic: Whether a re-read token list with duplicate agent names is accepted
questions: When a token-list re-read introduces duplicate agent names, especially with different author rights, is the new list accepted or rejected?

topics.topic: Whether run state is stored, cached, or derived from trace records
questions: Are run status, produced outputs and waiting points authoritative stored fields, cached projections, or always derived solely from trace records?

topics.topic: Whether successful trial responses include value outputs or only digests
questions: Does the MCP response for a successful trial return non-personal value outputs themselves or only their digests?
